newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends higher on trade buying.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends higher on trade buying.

text.p: CSCE world sugar ended higher on trade buying accompanied by scale-up selling by Brazilian producers, brokers said. Funds jumped into the act late in the session, but failed to trigger any stops.
The active October contract ended 0.06 cents higher at 11.67 cents a lb in a range of 11.56 to 11.68 cents a lb. The LIFFE October contract was 30 cents lower at $324.90.

"This is a market that's trending upward," said Walter Spilka, an analyst with Smith Barney. "The Thai crop is 14% smaller than last year. There's also some questions about the size of the Cuban crop."
Other traders noted that the Brazilian crop would offset any shortage of sugar from Thailand. The Brazilians have been hedge-sellers throughout the week.
Some traders noted the large speculative long position as reported in the Commodity Futures Trading Commission's commitment of traders.

"The number of fund longs in this market is absolutely enormous,"one said. "I have to think that the upside is limited. These funds are going to need to liquidate. They won't want a position too close to the spot month."
